chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Muhammad ibn al-Hasan ibn Shammun, from Abdullah ibn Abd al-Rahman al-Asam, from Misma' Abu Sayyar, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:
The Messenger of God (peace be upon him and his family) said: There is no emancipation except after ownership.

key_terms.عِتْق: Emancipation, manumission — the act of freeing a slave, a meritorious deed in Islamic law
key_terms.مِلْك: Ownership, possession — legal title to property; here referring to ownership of a slave

ai.seo_question: What did the Prophet say about the conditions for freeing a slave in Islam?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (AS) reports a ruling from the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) establishing that the act of freeing a slave (emancipation/manumission) is only legally valid if the person freeing the slave actually owns that slave. This principle prevents attempts to free slaves one does not possess, which would be legally meaningless. The ruling reflects a jurisprudential principle governing the conditions for valid manumission in Islamic law, where the act of emancipation requires the prerequisite of legitimate ownership.
